chunks.text: 40-year-old female, Associate Professional or Technician, resident of Sengkang, Singapore.
History of pneumonia resolved 5 years ago
Remote history of wrist fracture (healed) from 10 years ago
Previous diagnosis of mild iron deficiency anemia, resolved with dietary changes

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning! I'm going to be your anesthesiologist for your laparoscopic cholecystectomy tomorrow. I'd like to go through some questions to make sure we're all set for your surgery. Can you start by telling me a bit about why you're having this surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Sure. I've been having pain on the right side of my tummy, especially after eating. The doctor found a gallstone, and they said it's best to remove the gallbladder laparoscopically.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you. That helps. Now, let's go through your medications. I see you're on Atorvastatin, Lisinopril, Omeprazole, and Paracetamol as needed. Can you confirm if you're still taking all of these, and if not, when did you stop any of them?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I'm still taking Atorvastatin, Lisinopril, and Omeprazole every day. But I stopped taking Paracetamol already. I think it was about six months ago when my back pain got better.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great, thanks for clarifying that. Do you have any allergies? I see penicillin listed with a rash.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, I had a rash when I took penicillin before, so I avoid it. No other drug allergies that I know of.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. Are you currently on any other medications, supplements, or herbal remedies that aren't listed here?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I don't think so. Just the ones we already mentioned.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Let's talk about your health. You have a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and you're a bit overweight. How have those been managed lately?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: My blood pressure has been okay, not too high. I take Lisinopril regularly. Cholesterol is under control with Atorvastatin. And I know I need to lose some weight, but it's been hard.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thanks. Have you had any previous surgeries or anesthesia? Any problems with anesthesia in the past?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I had my wisdom teeth removed years ago, and that went fine. No problems with the anesthesia then.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. Are you currently on a NPO order? When was the last time you ate or drank anything?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I was told not to eat after midnight. I had some water until about 6 AM this morning, but nothing else.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect. Lastly, how would you describe your overall energy level and ability to perform daily activities?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I can do most things, but sometimes I get a bit tired, especially after meals. But I can walk, climb stairs, that sort of thing.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for all that information. We'll be using general anesthesia with a breathing tube for your surgery. We'll also give you some pain relief during and after surgery. Any questions for me?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I think that's all clear. I'm ready.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] induction propofol one hundred twenty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:02] fentanyl twenty micrograms

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] tube in, grade one view

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:07] rocuronium fifty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:15] 18 gauge IV line placed, 500 mL Ringer's Lactate bolus

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:30] mean arterial pressure dropped to fifty, atropine one milligram given

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [09:00] surgical incision, increase sevoflurane to two percent

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi there, how are you feeling after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: A bit sore, but okay lah. Still sleepy one.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's expected. On a scale of 0 to 10, how would you rate your pain right now?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Eh, maybe 4 or 5. My tummy is aching a bit, and I feel some burning from the tubes.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. Are you feeling nauseous or have you vomited at all since waking up?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No vomiting, but my stomach feels a bit uneasy. Like I might throw up if I move too much.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Okay, we can give you something for that. How’s your breathing? Any shortness of breath or discomfort?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Breathing is fine, but my throat is a bit sore from the tube, I think.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That can happen with the breathing tube. Do you remember anything from the operation itself?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I don’t remember anything. I just fell asleep and then woke up here.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. We’ll keep an eye on your blood pressure and overall condition. You have a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, so we’ll monitor those as well.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Okay, thank you. I hope I can go home soon.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: We’ll see how you progress. For now, rest and let the nurses know if you need anything.
